nodes.title: Run actionlint as a declared Bazel test
nodes.summary:
The original actionlint change is fully replaced by merged import #15250 at d3f4faffa. Upstream deliberately made the Bazel actions check optional, so default lint no longer requires host Bazel. The old default-lint failure is resolved. The Make-wrapper follow-up at 8f772e58b is retired as an unnecessary request; its source, validation refs and original failed-parent evidence are preserved. It was not landed. Complete six-path replacement review and independent peer 493c0a58dbdf closed; normal exact-lease remote deletion and named local deletion are verified (receipt bffaa781a15c). Only bazel-actionlint was retired; bazel-actionlint-ci remains preserved.

The reviewed actionlint correction is integrated in public, clean and tracked MAIN 1670b46d8ba7725ee2b3c7619951e216ba53ce00. Validation continuation 3f824ddf-8b12-40b3-ae4f-8f27fc12bb63 at unchanged fork source 8f772e58b6981a9e4c8da4acedebb2b89d1812b0 runs both selected test paths uncached: the canonical Docker-builder test passes in 20 ms, and explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false passes through RBE in 98 ms. Default evidence is the actual BEP/result output without materialized XML; the RBE result has its actual Action/Command/worker/log/XML join. Sealed outcome e6382a9238e1 retains the parent FAILED after 78.680 seconds solely because default-builder shutdown returns 2; both test phases and captures succeed, and final cleanup returns zero. That contributor request is now retired because the landed optional-check contract resolves its motivating default-lint failure. This does not claim a complete public import or full-CI pass.

The authorized October 2/3 rebase is published at e89cc398592a9e40b0d876bba1d2052e045d2314 on current master b65c70734a1bc7df49d000b911848b3ad2a9cce0. The requested attributed comment to @EtiennePerot is verified at https://github.com/google/gvisor/pull/15107#issuecomment-5963408537. Current checks and feedback are recorded in the GitHub snapshot; mergeability does not establish review or CI completion. Public older-source import #15250 at 263162ee3de76a03c0cd68da9f2eba16373201fe fails Buildkite 49348: the host lint step reports that Bazel is absent from PATH. The import contains older source 6db816c6c, while the live source PR remains e89cc3985. The owning correction delegates the actions check through canonical make test, preserving the default builder route and explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false. Its narrow source/record peer passed; the proposed wrapper is preserved as historical evidence. This failure does not establish that the unrelated Podman result has the same cause. The first hosted correction validation at fork source 8f772e58b6981a9e4c8da4acedebb2b89d1812b0 fails after 1,234.198 seconds (parent 65a1d557-984f-446c-a969-4818964d9ee3, sealed outcome 33eab553e459). The canonical builder image pull and container startup succeed, and Make reaches its TEST header; no actual Bazel test result is captured before the deadline and exit 137. The explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false phase never executes. Noninteractive post-timeout inspection can run Bazel 8.3.1 in the still-running builder. Cause is unproved; the later method-only continuation removes inherited terminal input and gives collection a separate bounded deadline. The coordinator reports Linux 5.15, distinct from the observed Linux 6.1 action workers; neither is evidence of a newer worker deployment. The original public import failure and this incomplete validation remain separate.

followup.nextAction: No follow-up is requested. Preserve the reviewed optional-wrapper source and historical validation evidence.

Canonical FIONREAD is zero; after clearing only ICANON, FIONREAD is six and one verified nonblocking read returns six M bytes (4d4d4d4d4d4d), instead of five M bytes plus newline. Recovery can advance delivery; exact corruption timing, deployed backport state and sole causal patch remain unproved. Nine passes are nonreproductions, not a fix or full PTY qualification. At that point a conditional provider draft was prepared; the complete current issue thread contains no posted follow-up from that draft.

Earlier kernel and capacity evidence: Supported worker-kernel selection remains unresolved; issue #13523 is open with no new provider resolution. Source-only review of the retained failed core run finds ten non-FIB netfilter validation failures consistent with older Linux behavior and dual-stack native/hostnet reservation failures matching Linux fix d9ba9934285514f1f95d96326a82398a22dc77f2. The failed execution's kernel build/configuration/backports remain unknown, so these are source/failure-pattern matches, not verified deployed-patch attribution. Nine FIB cases retain an unresolved module/configuration boundary. All original outcomes remain FAILED; no new job, expectation weakening or source fix was introduced. Session-keyring expectations have a separately validated fix; PTY and timestamp failures remain unresolved. The exact published text was read back. Provider response and deployment remain pending; no worker with the requested settings has been tested. The original case assertion fails in 3 ms. This supports the address-index omission fixed by upstream Linux 936a192f9, while the deployed worker source and backports remain unknown. The user approved the additional follow-up, and tamird posted it at 2026-10-02 16:38:40 UTC: https://github.com/buildbuddy-io/buildbuddy/issues/13523#issuecomment-5956862042. nodes.summary:
The complete ping pair timed out on both native host architectures at the original 300-second limits, in the first ICMPPortExhaustion case. Neither completed a case; 36 cases per owner were unstarted. Independent saved review bound both failures and the retained progress, without a speedup or cause claim. CPU attribution is being investigated separately. The earlier short mincore pilot remains a distinct two-host pass.

Earlier observations:

The paired mincore pilot passed both original 300-second actions, five cases on each native AMD64 and ARM64 OCI host. Independent review bound the 16 remotely inspected native tools, actual action inputs and byte-identical guest kernel, initramfs and payload. This short pair does not establish a speedup. The complete shared-filesystem ping pair is now accepted at eac536ce6 under its unchanged 300-second deadlines and full 37-case selection; its results are pending.

Earlier observations:

The resumed pilot passed graph routing and built both host archives, then its inspection step stopped on a BEP source-file path lookup before any TestRunner. The owner is preparing a narrow lookup correction; native-tool proof and guest execution remain unqualified. The source and guest choices are unchanged, and the partial evidence is being sealed.

Earlier observations:

The unchanged reviewed pilot resumed once at 588d3e6d3 after the pinned logical indexes became reachable again. Its original method, package checksum, exact-package fallback, two complete mincore targets and deadlines are unchanged. Results and native ARM64 host-tool proof remain pending; both prior zero-action failures are retained.

Earlier observations:

The reviewed source adds explicit ARM64-host tools for two existing complete mincore guests while preserving their payload, guest images and 300-second deadlines. Both pilot attempts stopped before execution. The first failed on the pinned AMD64 libexpat package. A single continuation used the standard Bazel exact-URL fallback; both official mirrors matched the existing package checksum. That continuation then failed when all four pinned jammy/main/amd64 package-index formats returned HTTP 503, before reaching the package fetch. There is no host-tool, ELF, placement, guest-runtime or timing result. Both saved failures are independently reviewed and retained. No further unchanged retry is planned while the immutable input prerequisite is unavailable. This fork pilot is not awaiting contributor review.

followup.disposition: Short pilot passed; full ping pair timed out

nodes.head: 715688f5dda713463b7ce4252ceab32eae3c2b26
nodes.title: BuildBuddy: retry canceled OCI initialization
nodes.summary:
BuildBuddy #13848 remains open and mergeable at 715688f5d. At October 18 13:28:06 UTC, sluongng left LGTM feedback as a COMMENTED review and asked for dan-stowell to review before merge; GitHub still reports REVIEW_REQUIRED, with bduffany and dan-stowell requested. At 13:49:15 UTC, sluongng linked their separate open PR #13851, which upgrades go-containerregistry to v0.22.1 and related dependencies; its current head is bf1f85f2e and review is required. No dependency change has been added to this branch. Public PR/build failed with a missing API key before any tests executed (exit 34). The Linux ARM64 lane passed both test targets, then failed its build-event upload with a missing API key (exit 38). Why the key was absent is unknown; these failures do not establish a source regression. CodeQL passed. The completed Windows executor job ran all five test targets: four passed and filecache_test timed out in both 60-second attempts (exit 1). Root recovered both Windows test logs and verified that filecache_test.go and BUILD match this PR head. Both attempts end during TestScanWithConcurrentAdd after 99 completed directory scans, with progress continuing until the 60-second timeout and no assertion failure. The test performs 100 trials of 100 files; its small size assigns a 60-second suite limit. Root found sluongng’s existing open PR #13781, which addresses this Windows concurrent-scan fixture problem. Its current head, 6867093386, has a passing Windows executor check. The Windows failure is linked to that existing work; no separate test-size proposal is being pursued. This evidence does not establish an OCI regression or a passing Windows result for #13848. Three Darwin ERROR statuses remain maintainer execution-approval gates, while hosted Linux/style/bare-metal/release statuses remain queued. The prepared real-registry regression fails before the correction and the corrected race suite passes 79 cases without skips; its connection to the hosted image-preparation incident remains unproved. Root reviewed the suggested go-containerregistry cleanup: later calls can reinitialize after a failure, while concurrent callers can still hold the canceled reader. That distinction is source-derived, not a new executed regression; the separate upgrade remains in sluongng’s PR #13851.

The contributor posted a follow-up at 17:33:41 UTC on October 18 asking whether any updates are needed. The current sweep found no incoming reply or review/check change. The separate authentication-evidence report remains unposted pending its existing authorization question.

followup.disposition: Existing Windows fixture fix, maintainer review and CI authentication pending
followup.nextAction: Track sluongng’s existing Windows fixture fix #13781, whose current head has a passing Windows executor check. nodes.head: d838db565fcf85d3caaf92ee0616fa08a1ddec51
nodes.title: Probe core scheduling support before testing it
nodes.summary:
Kernel versions do not establish whether core scheduling was built in or
whether SMT is active. Probe the current thread with a valid
`PR_SCHED_CORE_GET` before testing `Enable`, and skip only the
unsupported-operation and inactive-SMT errors. Unexpected GET errors and
every CREATE/SHARE error still fail the test.

Wrap the GET errno so the availability check can identify it through
`errors.Is`. The production `Enable` implementation is unchanged. Linux
gates `PR_SCHED_CORE` on `CONFIG_SCHED_CORE` and returns
`ENODEV` without active SMT.

nodes.head: aebc2c60a7ead4e32d5523edad54a0010123526a
nodes.title: Wait for fork setup before freezing children
nodes.summary:
The freezer tests could freeze a child before libc returned from
`fork()` and restored its temporary blocked signal mask. A subsequent
`SIGTERM` then stayed blocked, making the test report that the frozen
child failed to terminate. The `SIGQUIT` phase could also freeze before
the child installed its default disposition.

Wait for a readiness token after child setup and before freezing in both
fatal-signal tests. Keep the existing signal assertions, thaw behavior,
and deadlines.

investigations.title: CUBIC recovery and congestion-control testing
investigations.summary: The packet-level investigation found two RTT defects: loss probes admitted ambiguous samples, and RACK retained its lifetime minimum after the path grew longer. Both corrections have passing before/after packet regressions and affected unit/analyzer checks on AMD64 and ARM64. The contributor approved both: Karn is published as #15819, and the minimum-RTT correction awaits its merge. The first fixed two-host comparison shows a conditional 1.48% upload-throughput regression; download is inconclusive. The compact diagnostic representation now passes its selected unit, packet and analyzer checks. Actual layouts on both CPUs restore the inferred segment and sender heap slots to 256 and 896 bytes. The new fixed compact comparison completed all 52 processes and 96 measured bandwidth rows. Its equal-host aggregate intervals include zero for both Upload (+1.40%, 95% interval −0.0103% to +2.76%) and Download (+0.83%, −1.07% to +2.55%). Neither aggregate confidence interval excludes zero; this does not establish equivalence. The earlier upload regression remains a separate cohort; no historical samples are pooled. The approved source remains unchanged. The contributor approved compact amendment ca492fef9 after its exact range-diff; #15819 remains the upstream-submission prerequisite. Current Karn head a4eadcd7e is maintainer-approved, but Copybara import failed without a public diagnostic; the compact amendment remains held until the prerequisite actually merges.

findings.text: Isolated production-controller regressions reproduce two recovery behaviors: after a loss reduces the congestion window from 1000 to 700, ACKs covering 700 segments over 100 ms leave it at 700 for batch sizes 1, 2 and 10. With an aged epoch, one ACK instead moves it from 700 to 776. These are controller-arithmetic observations, not an end-to-end network reproduction.

A subsequent regression through the existing TCP sender packet path completes fast recovery, then observes a congestion window of 453 before and after a full window of ACKs. It uses the existing manual clock and Pause/Resume synchronization, without sleeps, a copied CUBIC formula or new production hooks. Broader impaired-link and performance conclusions require separate evidence.

A zero-new-ACK controller regression also observes growth from 700 to 1229. The first corrective validation reported passing targeted tests and analyzers after a test-fixture correction. This does not complete the wider recovery and performance investigation.

Existing infrastructure already provides paired Linux/netstack packetdrill targets and a TCP benchmark with network namespaces, netem and iperf. This work extends those routes and the existing manual-clock packet fixtures. The original packetdrill scripts cover basic connection/close behavior; the inspected SACK/RACK recovery cases use Reno by default.

The user-approved ACK-credit repairs are now Reno PR #15576 and CUBIC PR #15579. Both include the requested got/want assertion cleanup; CUBIC also includes the reviewed arithmetic simplification. The final CUBIC check passed ten named cases on each runtime architecture and both owning analyzer targets. The 32-bit saturation argument remains a source proof, not a new 32-bit runtime result. Earlier before failures and packet evidence remain retained; no contributor question is pending for either delivered change.

All 60 planned throughput trials were retained and independently checked against their source and helper binaries. At 100 Mbps, 100 ms RTT and configured 0.1% loss, original and first-ACK-repair CUBIC had receiver-goodput medians of 7.79 and 8.59 Mbps, but paired outcomes split three wins and three losses. This does not establish an improvement. Small-BDP controls reached 19.0–19.1 Mbps. These trials exclude the later idle, epoch and listener-inheritance changes; unseeded loss and queue drops limit interpretation.

The combined CUBIC ACK-credit, idle and epoch corrections with the Reno repair passed 11 selected unit, analyzer and packet target results, including normal and race configurations. The saved evidence supports this explicit target selection; the empty case XML provides no per-case census. Correctness success does not establish a throughput advantage.

Separate fast-recovery and retransmission-timeout smoke scripts passed on native Linux 6.1 and Netstack after selecting CUBIC directly on the accepted sending socket. The earlier Netstack scripts stopped before data transfer because accepted sockets reported Reno after the listener selected CUBIC. That inheritance defect remains separate from the four passing recovery targets.

The complete 35-flow study retained five functional controls and 30 balanced 120-second comparison flows. On one worker at 100 Mbps, 100 ms RTT and configured 0.01% loss, repaired CUBIC had median receiver goodput of 36.4 Mbps versus repaired Reno at 18.8 Mbps, with CUBIC higher in all six matched blocks. Original CUBIC had median 23.15 Mbps; the repaired bundle was higher in five of six pairs. Exact source, generated inputs and runtime binaries were independently joined. This source predates utilization and retransmission-cursor repairs. Unseeded loss and queue drops limit generalization; this does not reproduce the historical outage.

Two real-packet regressions keep two packets in flight after recovery, limited separately by the application and advertised receive window. Both originally grew the congestion window from 7 to 18. The correction now passes its effective 12-target test/analyzer selection after fixing an incompletely initialized unit fixture. Both the original growth failures and the intermediate fixture failures remain recorded. This establishes the selected correctness result, without a throughput or historical-outage reproduction claim.

findings.text: The user-approved accepted-socket inheritance repair is now PR #15574. Expected before failures and passing corrected unit, native, sandbox and analyzer targets remain recorded; the parent output-oracle failure is preserved. The user has requested maintainer review, and current-head GitHub checks and review are tracked on the PR.

Expanded RACK coverage reproduced an immediate duplicate segment after RTO with both original and corrected controllers. The sender-cursor repair passed 16 selected standalone-controller and integrated target results, including full SACK/RACK suites on both architectures, integrated TCP units, focused race tests, analyzers and formatting. Four existing RACK reorder-detection skips remain explicit. The original failures are retained. The user-approved cursor repair and independent SACK coverage are now PRs #15575 and #15577; the requested SACK arithmetic cleanup preserves the tested offsets.

evidence.label: Expanded recovery results with original failures

findings.text: The observation-harness functional check now retains per-stream receiver JSON and native ICMP observations before, during and after traffic. Five corrected client/server/both modes and the original no-probe mode passed; original startup failures remain recorded. Receiver totals and runtime helper identities were independently checked. These short checks establish instrumentation function, not comparative throughput, fairness, exact clock alignment or Netstack TCP RTT.

evidence.label: Original run with startup failures retained

findings.text: The final-controller matrix retained all 60 trials and independently joined their source, generated state, archives and actual helper binaries. At 100 Mbps, 100 ms RTT and configured 0.01% unseeded loss, repaired Netstack CUBIC exceeded repaired Netstack Reno in all six within-job pairs: median paired ratio 2.14×, range 1.62–2.36×. Repaired CUBIC also exceeded original CUBIC in all six pairs (median 1.75×), but remained below native Linux CUBIC in every pair (median 0.93×). The separate small-BDP controls are not pooled. Distinct job IDs do not establish physical-worker independence; these sequential single-flow measurements do not establish fairness, loaded latency, universal superiority or the historical outage cause.

Shared-flow functional validation is now closed. All 13 original normal modes passed, but the original expected-termination case omitted required inner cleanup records and its failed parent remains retained. A two-delimiter supervisor correction passed a normal mixed-flow control and the same termination case: both clients and flow supervisors were interrupted, both receivers were reaped, and both flow cleanups plus topology cleanup completed. Interrupted receivers do not count as completed traffic. This establishes functional capture and cleanup behavior, without a fairness, comparative-performance or precise-clock-alignment claim.

Independent review closes all 30 sharing trials and 60 raw receiver reports across three VM blocks. The original reader retained 27 observations and three analysis errors; the corrected saved-only reader preserves those 27 exactly and recovers the remaining three by bounding unlocated bytes and interval coverage. No workload was rerun. Native shared-path ICMP reports baseline median/p95 of 100 ms and loaded medians of 101–103 ms, with p95 of 105–109 ms. These are ICMP reply RTTs, not TCP RTT or pure queue delay.

All 12 matched-algorithm cross-stack trials are independently reviewed. Netstack’s share remains below half in every role-specific measurement bound, with Reno trial bounds spanning 24.0–32.8% and CUBIC bounds spanning 26.8–40.5%. These are ranges across individual observations, not pooled confidence intervals. The gap therefore persists without mixing algorithms, while its cause remains unresolved. Source inspection identified pre-existing work in disabled-probe snapshots; its performance impact has not been measured.

The original epoch qualification remains outcome unknown after its observation deadline: the service exposed no invocation or execution record and cancellation is unconfirmed. The corrected request, using exact public Git inputs instead of oversized embedded bodies, closed three expected before failures and passing full TCP unit and analyzer checks on both architectures. The epoch change is delivered as PR #15604. The separate disabled-probe comparison has completed; its source-bound interpretation remains separate from the earlier sharing studies.

In the epoch PR review, Etienne reported microbenchmark results for replacing math.Pow(t, 3) with multiplication: 13.670 to 1.912 ns and 12.625 to 1.934 ns, with 20 samples per version. The comment did not include benchmark source or environment. The user-authorized one-expression amendment is delivered at 98d5af4a3 after passing existing full TCP unit checks on AMD64 and ARM64 and the owning analyzers. The reply was posted and the thread is resolved.

The source-isolated SACK accounting study completed all 24 instrumented shared-WAN trials on three workers, with controllers and workload held fixed and four accounting production files changed. Original outputs and source joins were collected; this historical observation does not supply an independent result assessment. Separately, RACK initialization checks reproduced high/wrapped-ISN failures at manual-clock time zero, with a passing low-ISN control. The correction passed eight selected targets and is delivered as PR #15618. The user-approved follow-up RTTSeq amendment is also delivered at 0a0e6fc2a, with its reply posted and thread resolved.

The sender-owner prototype passed its remote correctness checks. All eight paired WAN trials completed. Three of four Netstack-share change bounds include zero; the CUBIC-primary pair fell from 28.43–33.25% to 21.74–24.83%. These are conservative measurement bounds on one worker, not statistical confidence intervals or proof of a causal regression.

findings.text: Existing packetimpact limitations are preserved from the reference-mode f47c93525 run: TestPAWSMechanism and TestTimeWaitReset fail on Netstack, together with six RACK cases—TestRACKTLPAllPacketsLost, TestRACKTLPLost, TestRACKWithLostRetransmission, TestRACKWithReorder, TestRACKWithSACK and TestRACKWithoutReorder. These are known limitations under the established policy, not newly introduced regressions or an established cause of the separate sharing gap.

findings.text: The sender-owner follow-up, Actions 38170613265 on source 3a8358346, completed four original 120-second CUBIC flows with both sender roles and balanced AB/BA order. Its standard pprof decoder continuation 43589ae4 completed successfully and is independently reconciled with the original profiles. Each whole-client profile has 210–239 samples, representing 2.10–2.39 CPU seconds over roughly 121 seconds. These samples do not establish total CPU saturation or a causal explanation for sharing, and do not measure waiting time, short bursts, scheduler delay or controller-only cost. The earlier 0eedd2d5 decoder attempt remains UNKNOWN and was not rerun.

The first Nagle/full-MSS candidate 85c77c20 remains a failed, fixture-limited result; its source, native and core-report verification is now closed. Its GSO cases stopped before send assertions and retain no GSO correctness credit. Continuation fc902df4 corrected the common checksum and RACK timing fixtures and closed the bounded sender/packet validation. The final helper revision then replaced the rejected cleanup pattern with the borrowed AsView API introduced by #15635, and after-only validation 82940fa9 closed the full affected E2E owners and owning analyzers. Earlier before and RACK packet evidence remain tied to their actual sources. The standalone proposal 1c68399f1 is contributor-approved and depends on PR #15635 landing. This establishes no throughput advantage, physical GSO segmentation result, fresh standalone build or internal minRTT-cause diagnosis.

findings.text: The RACK fixture is extracted at fbf0f19b1 without changing the qualified packet-test body. It derives payload size from the negotiated MSS, checks complete retransmissions, acquires cleanup immediately and allows the delayed retransmission ACK to settle. The production RACK changes are comments only. Removing the expected-failure marker depends on the separate Nagle/GSO runtime correction; no fresh standalone execution is claimed.

evidence.label: Combined Linux and Netstack packet validation

findings.text: Diagnostic 684e619be and qualified composition 2fa25f3b6 exercise the production RACK update, reordering-window and loss-detection path. After an initial 10 ms sample and six 100 ms samples spanning more than 360 seconds, the lifetime minimum remains 10 ms and the reordering window 2.5 ms. The timer marks the original lost at 103.5 ms; its modeled unretransmitted ACK at 110 ms establishes reordering. Unchanged-path and two high-then-low controls avoid loss before their 12 ms ACK. All fourteen selected RACK entries per CPU and both analyzer wrappers pass. The fixture models ACK timing rather than executing full sender recovery; its high-then-low cases do not establish delayed-ACK eligibility across expiration.

Independent review of all 59 original files and 29 source bodies closes the actual ACK-accounting diagnostic on both architectures. Six 100 ms samples after a 10 ms seed leave a 2.5 ms reordering window; the SACK/timer path retransmits before the modeled original ACK at 110 ms. No-timestamp ACKs after a tail loss probe also change SRTT from 10 ms to 15 ms or 9.375 ms, exposing a separate Karn violation. The lone-runt receiver delay is modeled, not an observed receiver policy.

The standalone loss-probe RTT correction moves measurement invalidation from resendSegment into sendSegment’s retransmission branch. Identical packet fixtures fail against the original production code only for ambiguous no-timestamp ACKs. Corrected ACK and RACK suites and owning analyzers pass on AMD64 and ARM64; the existing DSACK skip remains. Timestamp-identified samples and later new-data samples remain eligible. Original outputs and compiled-source identities were independently reviewed. The final message-only amendment preserves the executed source.

evidence.label: Loss-probe RTT correction awaiting contributor review

findings.text: The minimum-RTT correction now passes the complete selected ACK histories on both architectures, including sustained longer-path/reordered-original delivery and low-path return. The first run’s two fixture failures came from an unintended 20 ms loss probe before their 50 ms ACK. The corrected fixtures ACK at 15 ms and 30 ms and require zero retransmissions; a focused continuation passes. Unchanged private TCP/RACK and analyzer results remain applicable, including the existing DSACK skip. Independent source and original-result reviews are complete. The final one-commit tree is identical to the tested source. The filter adds fixed sender state and two fields per segment; exact layout and throughput effects remain unmeasured.

Corrected packet fixtures and analyzer continuation

findings.text: The third benchmark submission completed all 52 fresh processes: four warmups and 48 measured processes, yielding 96 Upload/Download bandwidth rows. Original logs, fresh process results, opposite starting orders and arithmetic are independently checked. Both versions include Karn and differ by the approved minimum-RTT correction. The fixed paired-block analysis estimates upload throughput down 1.48% (pointwise 95% interval: -2.51% to -0.33%); download is inconclusive (+1.89%, -0.58% to +4.90%). Per-host unpaired benchstat detects neither difference. The hosts use different AMD EPYC models, so the aggregate is conditional on these two cohorts and assumes independent balanced blocks; it is not an equivalence claim. Actual Go 1.27.2 layouts imply segment heap slots grow from 256 to 288 bytes and sender slots from 896 to 1,024 bytes. These are allocator-class inferences, not measured per-packet allocations. The two earlier setup failures produced no samples and remain separate.

The compact representation at eed3f29ed passes six semantic owners and three analyzer wrappers, including all three split/ACK witness cases on both CPUs. The two existing DSACK-related skips remain explicit; there is no race phase. Actual matched Sentry layouts on AMD64 and ARM64 imply 256-byte segment and 896-byte sender heap slots, restoring the baseline classes. These are allocator-class inferences, not per-packet allocation measurements. The new fixed two-host comparison uses matched runtime sources in 7c79da672 and bdc691f3c, with Karn in both arms, twelve balanced pairs per host, opposite starting orders and 96 primary bandwidth rows. Actions 38839701028 completed; its verified throughput results are recorded below, without historical sample pooling. The approved proposal remains 7e371d8ac.

evidence.label: Focused correctness and matched layout evidence

findings.text: The compact RACK comparison completes all 52 fresh benchmark processes, including four warmups and 48 measured processes with 96 primary bandwidth rows. Original native PASS results, empty-but-clean XML reports, exact balanced order and private-daemon controls verify. Both runner cohorts record AMD EPYC 9V74 processors with four logical CPUs. The fixed equal-host paired-block analysis gives Upload +1.40% (pointwise 95% interval −0.0103% to +2.76%) and Download +0.83% (−1.07% to +2.55%). Neither aggregate interval excludes zero. Host 0 alone shows an upload gain; host 1 does not. This is not an equivalence result, and it does not establish behavior on lossy or changing paths. Historical samples are not pooled, and differences from the earlier cohort are not attributed to the compact representation alone. Source, native executable inputs and matched layouts are independently verified. The measured AMD64 segment and sender heap classes match the Karn-only baseline. Earlier separate qualification covers both architecture layouts; this throughput cohort is AMD64 only.

investigations.title: pkg/state: code generation and generics design
investigations.summary:
The complete integrated state proposal 3a38641f0 now has a matched comparison against its current prerequisite base. Exact arms fdc73917e and 6b522949e share the same fixtures and qualification infrastructure; twelve balanced adjacent pairs across four Save/Load fixtures produced 104 fresh children, including 96 measured observations. UDP Save is 10.73% faster, UDP Load is 14.44% faster, and adoption Load is 7.89% faster (all p<.001). Adoption Save timing is inconclusive (p=.060). UDP Save allocated bytes fall by 21.34% and UDP Load bytes by 14.96%, with allocation counts unchanged. Adoption Save uses 2.53% fewer bytes and 12.94% fewer allocations; adoption Load uses 7.07% fewer bytes and 17.93% fewer allocations. Wire sizes are unchanged. These results compare the full proposal with its prerequisite base; earlier scalar-stage samples remain separate. The matched startup run also passed: CLI medians are 2.380 versus 2.397 ms (p=.410), and StartupEmpty medians are 283.7 versus 265.8 ms (p=.198); neither establishes a timing difference. State initialization remains 3,032 bytes and 13 allocations in both runsc and Sentry. Production file growth is 98,304 bytes for AMD64 runsc, 253,952 for AMD64 Sentry, 131,072 for ARM64 runsc and 262,144 for ARM64 Sentry. The complete proposal packet is published, and the contributor review request is pending. Upstream submission also requires #15648 and #15814 to land. These are publication holds: the qualified fork already contains both prerequisite compositions. Its shared graph/wire representation, typed captures and checked bulk array restore have complete current-consumer, aggregate and startup evidence. The bounded follow-up assessment found no new concrete hypothesis or missing experiment; further architecture work remains authorized when there is a specific question to test.

Integrated proposal and earlier source-specific evidence:

The integrated state proposal is published at 3a38641f0 on diagnostics/state-integrated-array-proposal. It combines the qualified scalar-helper deletion and typed-array representation on current upstream 1a256dc06 with the existing #15648 and #15814 prerequisites. Independent export review accounts for all 44 proposal paths and the preserved build adapters. Its fresh current-consumer composition passes four AMD64/ARM64 runsc and Sentry builds plus two checkpoint/cycle smoke owners with nine passing entries. The previous aggregate 67c4ddcf6 remains preserved. Compare the single commits with git range-diff 67c4ddcf6^! 3a38641f0^!; the earlier 00d19e629 comparison is also retained. The complete proposal still needs matched prerequisite-base timing and startup assessment; the published typed-array timing gains remain specific to its scalar control.

Previous source-specific typed-array comparison:

The fixed typed-array comparison is complete on scalar control cca2fa281 versus production candidate 7eda99c92. Twelve balanced adjacent pairs across four complete Save/Load fixtures produced 104 fresh children, including 96 measured observations, without pooling earlier samples. UDP32 Load is 13.61% faster and adoption Load is 5.54% faster (both p<.001); the two Save timing differences are inconclusive (p=.514 and .060). Load allocated bytes fall by 14.96% and 7.07%, respectively. Adoption Load allocations fall by 17.93%; UDP32 Load allocations are unchanged. Repeated UDP32 Save adds one allocation (p=.009); its 27-byte median increase is inconclusive (p=.139). The separate one-operation UDP32 Save observation remains +576 bytes and one fewer allocation. The qualified file-size costs remain: +36,864 bytes per AMD64 binary, +65,536 bytes for ARM64 runsc, and unchanged ARM64 Sentry. The two setup failures ran no measured children and remain recorded. These are complete-fixture Load improvements against the scalar candidate. Startup and whole checkpoint/restore effects on this candidate remain unmeasured.

Separately qualified allocation and file-size observations:

The typed-array prototype at 7eda99c92 passes a combined nineteen semantic, race and analyzer owners with 33,046 passing XML entries, plus four production links. Its original static-check failures remain recorded; the continuation moves unchanged unsafe restore functions to their existing owner file and uses a tagged switch in the fixture. Complete one-operation allocation observations against scalar control cca2fa281 show adoption Load using 18,368 fewer bytes and 1,023 fewer allocations. UDP32 Load uses 33,728 fewer bytes but one additional allocation; UDP32 Save adds 576 bytes and removes one allocation. Empty, ordinary and control-message observations are unchanged, and wire sizes remain equal. Five existing baseline observations were reused; only the previously missing UDP32 Load baseline was run. Each AMD64 runsc/Sentry file grows by 36,864 bytes; ARM64 runsc grows by 65,536 bytes and Sentry is unchanged. These observations establish neither latency benefit nor readiness. The validated aggregate 67c4ddcf6 remains a separate design proposal.

Earlier source-specific experiments:

The isolated scalar-helper deletion at 543d8d692c passes eleven semantic, race and analyzer owners with 32,925 passing XML entries, plus four production links. In the matched one-operation allocation observations, empty, ordinary, adoption and control-message Save costs are unchanged; UDP32 Save uses 1,408 fewer bytes and 94 fewer allocations with the same 13,179 wire bytes. Compared with the qualified 2b05 composition, AMD64 runsc and Sentry files each shrink by 24 KiB, ARM64 runsc by 64 KiB, and ARM64 Sentry is unchanged. These are allocation and file-size observations, not timing, startup or whole-workflow results. The simplification remains diagnostic; aggregate proposal 67c4ddcf6 and its source-specific performance limits are preserved.

The aggregate state design proposal at 67c4ddcf6 now passes fresh current-consumer integration on composition 2b05eaf212. The canonical producer reports PASS for four AMD64/ARM64 runsc and Sentry builds plus two fresh TestDeadlock/TestCheckpointRestore processes, with nine passing XML entries, no failures or skips, and unchanged source and lockfile. The original zero-process loading failure remains recorded. The complete export retains 44 of the 45 qualified changed paths, excluding only the three-line diagnostic empty benchmark leaf; both adapted build owners are included. The exact proposal comparison remains git range-diff 00d19e629^! 67c4ddcf6^!, with open #15648 and #15814 prerequisites. This closes consumer compilation and checkpoint smoke, not performance readiness. Earlier source-specific comparisons have not demonstrated an end-to-end timing gain, and residual binary growth remains. The aggregate remains an agent-owned design proposal; no contributor-review or upstream-submission request is pending.

Earlier source-specific qualification and measurements:

findings.text: The current generator emits Save/Load calls with addresses of statically known fields. Sink.Save and Source.Load then accept any and reconstruct reflect.Values. The prototype will retain that known type information in generated field operations while sharing the existing wire/type/identity/wait graph. AST spelling alone is insufficient for imported, aliased or shadowed types; the generator needs a sound type proof or a compatible dynamic fallback.

At the studied Go 1.27.1 pin, the specification and compiler support generic methods. Array lengths still require constant expressions, and generic code is not automatically devirtualized. Language feasibility therefore does not establish an allocation or timing benefit.

Pointer identity, cycles, interior aliases, overlapping slices and delayed load callbacks must retain their semantics under one graph mechanism. Those requirements do not make reflective field traversal unavoidable: generated descriptors and typed operations can carry known representation information. The prototype must preserve registration before reentrant hooks and distinct aggregate storage where callbacks retain addresses; compatibility for arbitrary dynamic types remains part of the design.

The initial prototype specializes proved scalar/pointer fields and uses typed allocation and assignment while retaining the same wire and object-identity/wait graph. Pointer identity metadata still traverses the current reflective boundary. A later descriptor-based encoder could discover and snapshot objects once, then emit finalized IDs without boxing every wire value; it must cache hook/SaveValue results and captured values because callbacks and slice-tail clearing can mutate state. This is a design direction, not an executed performance result.

findings.text: Existing whole-restore logs place kernel loading around 23–27 ms, including statistics formatting; broader timers overlap and cannot be added. investigations.title: pkg/state: reflection CPU and allocation profiles
investigations.summary:
The recorded profiling and fixed comparisons are complete. Their mixed and negative results remain below; the subsequent decoded-frame qualification and architecture experiments continue in the separate state design investigation. This profiling record has no pending execution or contributor decision.

The completed pointer experiments remain unpromoted: the first coherent-pointer comparison had five timing regressions, two gains and twelve nonsignificant results; the enclosing-pointer comparison had three regressions, four gains and twelve nonsignificant results. Earlier helper, map-registration and reader experiments remain separate evidence.

The generated restore successor is now implemented and independently correctness-qualified. It uses one authoritative graph pointer and a static restoration callback, shared map/array ordering, typed destination operations and exact registered-type callback selection. Four corrected full suites plus eighteen retained owners and two production links pass; thirteen serialized streams match across four groups. Original shared-fixture construction failures remain recorded. Runtime-sized slice backing retains the existing reflection boundary.

Its fixed comparison is mixed and unpromoted: five Load timing gains, two adoption slowdowns and twelve nonsignificant timings across 52 actions and 456 rows. Load allocations fall, while the state and UDP test executables grow 19.54% and 25.48%. The separate RestoreEmpty pilot passes all six save/load iterations, with overlapping Load ranges and a 21.50% larger runsc; three CPUID-warmed operations per arm are descriptive, not a significance or cold-start result.

A separate two-line shared-envelope consolidation at b941f2f056 passes six owners and four matched executable checks. It reduces runsc by 1,634,304 bytes on AMD64 and 1,507,328 bytes on ARM64 relative to the measured successor. Timing was not rerun, so this size result does not remove the earlier performance limitations. A further shared-struct helper at 2831e4a8e2 passes six owners and three groups of thirteen matching streams. Its matched executables shrink again relative to b941: runsc by 1,814,528 bytes on AMD64 and 1,507,328 bytes on ARM64. The subsequent fixed shared-struct comparison is independently closed and still mixed: nine timing gains, three regressions and seven nonsignificant results. Focused captured/uncaptured adoption profiles are also closed. Array restoration occupies 42.58% and 46.08% cumulative CPU in the candidate profiles, including nested restoration, statistics and waits; those overlapping sampled totals do not identify reflection alone as the cause or predict a speedup. No successor is proposed for adoption.

The runtime-array revision at e0515a1d8b has a fully reviewed fixed comparison against coherent control 225fdf9301. It shows five Load timing gains, a 3.54% UDP Save regression (p=.039), and thirteen nonsignificant timings. Captured and uncaptured adoption Load medians rise 2.62% and 3.45%, respectively, without statistical significance; that does not establish equivalence. The state and UDP test executables grow 50.24% and 59.79%. This revision remains unpromoted.

The shared array-loop/view revision at 173993df1f passed six test/analyzer owners and three groups of thirteen matching streams. Its state and UDP test executables are 8,573,088 and 8,994,976 bytes, down 5.42% and 5.87% from e051. Its original production-link deadline is retained separately from the completed link continuation. The subsequent shared-pointer helper at fffd29842d6d passed the focused correctness checks and production links. Its runsc executables are 54,141,088 bytes on AMD64 and 50,790,560 bytes on ARM64. The AMD64 executable remains 37.23% larger than the retained coherent control (39,452,832 bytes); the production comparison has a recorded version-stamp input difference and is not a byte-attribution or startup claim.

The shared-pointer fixed comparison 8ae794ca is independently closed: seven timing gains, five regressions and seven nonsignificant results. Captured and uncaptured adoption Load regress 4.60% and 6.91%; state and UDP test executables remain 38.29% and 46.16% larger than the matched coherent control. This mixed result remains unpromoted.

The earlier shared-pointer idle-Nginx restore pilot remains independently confirmed incomplete: each arm produced two one-iteration observations, then the third restore failed during Docker/containerd checkpoint upload. The four observed rows do not complete the required six-row pilot. Native exit status, BEP and parent status incorrectly reported success despite benchmark failure text and XML failures; the original discrepancy is retained. It supplies no complete end-to-end comparison or adoption claim.

The data-plan successor at 221124de7 is independently correctness-qualified. Its fixed comparison has seven timing regressions, one gain and eleven nonsignificant results, and remains unpromoted. State/UDP test executables grow 2.64%/2.81%; matched runsc files grow 2.41% on AMD64 and 2.48% on ARM64. Reviewed diagnostic profiles identify per-Load metadata construction and recurring dispatch/parsing costs without proving causal effect sizes. A separate Nginx pilot completes three actual restores per arm; overlapping small-sample timings do not establish a performance improvement.

The metadata-ownership revision at 5401bbaba is independently qualified for the selected correctness and race checks, with three groups of thirteen streams matching the prior data-plan source. Single measured-Load allocation reductions are observed, alongside increased initialization allocation counts. The adoption fixture uses Save-only setup, but ControlMessageDecoding performs an untimed validation Load before measurement; its row is not a first-use layout cost. Each timing has only one observation, so these measurements do not establish a timing improvement. Production executable sizes are unchanged from 221124de7 and remain about 2.4% larger than the coherent control. The candidate remains unpromoted.

The fixed idle-Nginx comparison of metadata-ownership source 5401bbaba against coherent control 3aa3a761c is independently closed: all twenty-four actual checkpoint-and-restore operations completed, twelve per arm, each starting a fresh sentry. Median observed time rises from 0.876 seconds to 1.157 seconds (31.98%). The measurement includes restore and port-presence detection, not HTTP readiness or populated traffic. Repetitions share one worker per arm, so worker effects remain uncontrolled and the difference cannot be attributed solely to code. The candidate remains unpromoted.

The control-message observation uses 96 more bytes with the same 102 allocations after an untimed validation Load; it is not a first-use layout cost. Initialization totals are unchanged. Test executable file lengths are unchanged, with text sections 192 bytes larger. Single measured-load observations and the closed diagnostic profiles do not establish a latency improvement; the candidate remains experimental and unpromoted.

The byte-reader comparison is independently closed. On the deterministic synthetic pointer/slice graph through the real uncompressed statefile reader, twelve fixed balanced pairs show no detected time benefit (median 766,202.5 to 760,387 ns, p=.198), 16 additional bytes per operation and unchanged 4,953 allocations per operation. All twenty-six native processes exited successfully, with twenty-four measured rows; the original parent failure and XML reporter errors remain recorded. These saved measurements were authenticated without rerunning benchmarks. This is not a whole-kernel restore or fresh-sentry startup measurement. The byte-reader revision remains unpromoted.

The decoded-frame architecture uses one parser and generated restoration methods. Both stable-block and inline candidates remain unadopted. The simpler contiguous revision passes correctness and its fixed comparison: large synthetic Load is 19.00% faster with 36.85% fewer allocated bytes, while control-message timing has no detected change. Executable file sizes are unchanged. Independent review is complete. The completed 24-operation whole-restore comparison does not establish an overall speedup. Subsequent profiling and the unsuccessful type-description sharing experiment are recorded in the design investigation; no successor has been adopted.

findings.text: Map reflection was the strongest measured reflection opportunity. In sampled allocation-object profiles, reflect.unsafe_New accounted for 51.12% flat in Map Load and 25.41% flat in Map Save. Map Save also spent 25.13% cumulative CPU in MapKeys and 15.24% in MapIndex; cumulative entries overlap and must not be added.

Other costs would survive simply replacing reflective field access: Stats.sample accounted for 21.24% cumulative CPU in Pointer Load, while the 32-packet UDP Save profile attributed 40.06% of sampled allocation objects to wire.Struct.Alloc and 26.53% to encodeStruct. Sample percentages are estimates, not exact allocation counts or predicted savings.

All five profiling actions completed, but the original parent failed because its collector expected a ZIP. The ten individual CPU/heap files were retained and decoded in a tool-only continuation, with no benchmark repetition. The original failed parent remains failed.

Independent saved-result review verified all 192 measured rows, 12 balanced AB/BA pairs and the actual source-to-binary inputs. Map Save medians were 240.95 versus 214.75 ns per normalized unit (benchstat −10.87%, p=.020, 12 samples per side); allocated bytes were 156 versus 129 (−17.31%). None of the seven other timing comparisons was statistically significant in this run; this does not establish equivalence. The production difference is only the delivered MapRange loop.

Source review withdrew the first one-line decoder preallocation candidate before testing. Normal referenced maps are eagerly allocated in decodeObject before decodeMap, so adding a size hint only in decodeMap misses the owning allocation path. No preallocation measurements were run; the next candidate must address the actual map-creation path.

evidence.label: Decoder allocation ownership in the measured cohort

findings.text: The struct/header coallocation experiment changes only encode.go and wire.go against the fixed-work baseline. Independent review verified 264 measured rows and 12 balanced before/after pairs per cohort. Control-message Save uses 11.76% fewer allocations; UDP queue Save uses 12.83%, 19.03% and 20.30% fewer at 1, 8 and 32 packets. All eleven timing comparisons are nonsignificant (smallest p=.060). Allocated bytes are essentially unchanged and serialized sizes are identical. This remains an experiment, not a ready PR or checkpoint-speedup claim.

Reusing decoder temporary key/value slots outside Struct and Array kinds reduced the fixed 1024-entry Map Load median from 449,457 to 368,672 ns (-17.97%, benchstat p<.001, n=12). Allocated bytes fell 6.71% and allocations fell 52.47%. Root verified the original 192 measured rows and 12 pairs. Only decode.go differs between the measured inputs; the seven other timing comparisons were nonsignificant.

Reusing scalar iterator storage reduced the separate fixed 1024-entry Map Save median from 195,068 to 184,478.5 ns (-5.43%, benchstat p=.010, n=12). Allocated bytes fell 6.17% and allocations fell 35.82%; seven other timing comparisons were nonsignificant. The original measured rows and numeric interpretation are independently reviewed. MapRange #15542 subsequently landed, and the contributor-approved iterator-storage change is delivered as PR #15621.

The shared-primitive prototype at 74c23e08a passed the selected five-owner compatibility scope. In the paired study, pointer Load improved by 7.72% (p=.002); the other eight timing changes were not significant, and allocation counts did not change. Executable size still increased: UDP by 15% and state by 7.1%. CPU/heap capture and pointer-only controls have since completed. Direct generated emission is now the primary architectural experiment; this shared-primitive prototype is not an upstream-ready proposal.

evidence.label: Completed CPU and heap profile capture

findings.text: The first direct framed prototype is public at b83596347, with qualification e0292b990. It captures generated primitive fields directly and retains the existing graph, hooks and deferred reference ownership. The appended experimental format is opt-in; older readers do not support it. Correctness run 2b48aa70 passed all five runtime actions and three analyzers. Two analyzers failed on an unused initial Scalar value at framed_unsafe.go:51; the failed parent is retained. An initializer-only continuation f34a56f9 completed successfully. The subsequent paired framed measurements are complete and reported separately below.

The direct framed experiment regressed all nine timing comparisons (p<.001). At 32 queued UDP packets, Save time increased 24.98%, allocated bytes increased 69.05%, and wire bytes increased 16.76%, even though allocation count fell 41.48%. Pointer Load took 40.86% more time. Root verified these values against the original benchstat output. The process-level RSS observations do not establish an improvement. This slower prototype is not an upstream proposal; the owner subsequently completed the six-operation RestoreEmpty compatibility pilot and hotspot profiles. That pilot also had worse timing/image size and is not a statistical performance comparison. Subsequent existing-wire and direct-layout measurements also failed to establish an overall speedup; their results remain separate.

The first existing-wire direct-storage experiment preserves wire size but regresses UDP Save time by 6.69% and allocated bytes by 8.80%, despite 35.69% fewer allocations. Control-message Save/Load regress 63.85%/104.48%. The follow-up layout experiment also shows no speedup: UDP time is not significant (p=.068), allocations fall 37.21% while bytes rise 7.31%, and control Save/Load regress 14.10%/24.74%. These are separate matched 12-pair experiments; their timings are not comparisons across workers. Neither design is ready for upstream.

The independent primitive-array prototype keeps the Array wire grammar and copies captured values into owned storage. The actual addressable-versus-value fixture failed for signaling float32 NaNs before correction; complex64 matched. Corrected source cd66d9b1dd stores the float32 promotion in owned float64 values. All 11 selected targets passed, including baseline state, corrected state/wire on both CPUs, state race and five analyzers. Original outputs and source captures are bound. The paired result is complete: UDP Save time fell 11.88% (p<.001), allocated bytes fell 21.34%, and allocation count/wire size were unchanged. Pointer Save/Load rose 2.75%/2.20% (p=.033/.017); six other timings were not significant. Executables grew less than 1%, and no process-RSS benefit is established. The observed wire.Save dispatch shape changed, but that is not a proven cause of the timing regressions. A narrow default-arm refinement at d837b98735 is now under separate correctness validation. Its integration state.go/types.go differ from current master; the exact-current-package repeat is now independently reviewed. It improves UDP Save time 11.51% (p<.001) and allocated bytes 21.31%, with unchanged count/wire. Pointer Load improves 3.07% (p=.002), Map Load regresses 0.59% (p<.001), and six other timings are not significant. All 11 current-source correctness/analyzer targets passed. Root has now asked for contributor review of exact standalone 3b13f133c. Its per-arm wire size is 12,873 bytes and allocation count is 3,623, unchanged within that repeat; the earlier integration cohort used different absolute values.

The save-side legacy-byte capture experiment passed correctness but is rejected on its measured performance. In 12 paired comparisons (216 measured rows), UDP Save time rose 18.51%, allocated bytes rose 42.10% and allocation count rose 21.56%; wire size stayed 12,873 bytes. This compares modes in the same source containing the new plumbing, not the genuine unmodified parent. The separate checkpoint compatibility pilot passed six restore operations, but three operations per arm with the same reported executor-worker ID do not establish a timing effect or identical VM/CPU placement. The closed allocation profiles identify piece growth and per-struct capture storage as added costs. They are process-wide sampled estimates, not exact per-operation allocation accounting. No upstream proposal or speedup claim follows from this result.

Explicit type-owned registration corrects promoted snapshot dispatch on embedding parents. In e6dfccc3, both old snapshot leaves fail while their two legacy controls pass; all ten corrected owners pass, covering full state/wire on both CPUs, race and five analyzers. The original expected failed parent and zero cleanup/restoration status are retained. The earlier b8940bc2 nine-target pass lacked these embedding regressions and remains limited to its original fixture scope. No performance result follows from this correction.

This one-worker, pinned-logical-CPU experiment establishes neither cross-machine equivalence nor retained-heap or startup benefits. Matched runsc executable files grow 2.41% on AMD64 and 2.48% on ARM64 versus the coherent control. The complete design remains unpromoted; file growth is not attributed to individual mechanisms.

investigations.title: Scheduled tracker refresh reliability
investigations.summary:
The default-branch workflow now requests full refreshes every ten minutes. The unchanged collector uses 19 requests and 112 GraphQL points per sweep; six runs per hour fit the conservative 1,000-point workflow-token budget. The revised workflow passed all 29 JavaScript and 33 Python checks and published a live-verified snapshot. GitHub had not created runs for the first two revised slots by 05:10 UTC, so unattended scheduling reliability remains unverified. Active ownership now checks for ten-minute staleness and an existing queued or running refresh before using the same manual dispatch.

Before the correction, the active default-branch workflow requested runs at minutes 18 and 48, but the eight observed scheduled runs were created two to four hours apart. Their creation and start timestamps matched, which locates the observed gap before job execution. No disabled workflow, inactive repository, wrong default branch or inactive actor was found; the provider cause remains unknown. GitHub documents that scheduled events can be delayed or dropped. Manual refreshes do not establish a scheduler repair.

findings.text: At the 11 October schedule audit, the default-branch workflow was configured for minutes 18 and 48 of each UTC hour. The latest scheduled run observed by that audit was created at 01:01:30 UTC on 11 October and completed the 01:03:14 snapshot in status-only commit 560dd0edb. That newer automated snapshot was preserved before the curated update. Five earlier scheduled runs succeeded on 10 October, created at 01:18, 07:45, 13:59, 18:39 and 22:00 UTC. Successful execution is established, but the observed multi-hour gaps before event creation do not demonstrate regular 30-minute cadence. Their cause remains unexplained.

The configuration and run-history audit found no disabled workflow, wrong default branch, blocked job or queued run explaining the gap. The missing events occur before job execution, so there is no failed job log identifying their cause. No replacement scheduler or repeated re-registration has been introduced.

GitHub documents that scheduled jobs can be delayed or dropped. That is a service limitation, not proof of this gap’s cause. Manual publication through the existing collector is keeping verified snapshots visible while regular automatic cadence remains unproven.

The October 15 scheduled refresh collected successfully but lost a publication race to a metadata update. Workflow acffb2cb5 now recollects on the latest site revision after a confirmed concurrent update. The validation run reproduced that race and published on its second attempt; Pages deployed the new snapshot while preserving the README update. Authentication or transport failure against an unchanged remote head still fails the job.

The request-limit failure came from repeatedly fetching terminal source and import history. The corrected collector uses a complete open-PR inventory to discover reopening, confirms closures of previously active records, and refreshes known active imports even under terminal sources. Thirty Python regression cases run before snapshot collection in Actions. The successful live run used 20 requests and preserved 131 terminal-source observation clocks; historical terminal details do not acquire a fresh timestamp.

The enabled workflow on the actual default branch schedules minutes 18 and 48 each UTC hour. The 17 October audit found no newer scheduled event after the successful 00:31 run through 03:29 UTC, despite valid configuration and no queued or disabled job. A scheduled run subsequently resumed at 05:02:07 UTC and succeeded, producing the 05:02:58 full GitHub snapshot. That snapshot is preserved in the published site. The earlier missing events have no job log identifying their cause, which remains unknown; one successful resumed run does not establish regular 30-minute cadence. Event sweeps retain their separate observation clocks.

Resumed scheduled refresh and preserved full snapshot

findings.text: Scheduled run 39086958437 used master head 8d4b0fa81, completed successfully, and published status-only Pages commit 5cf5886b85. The adopted snapshot has no new actionable source/import events compared with the preceding verified owner update. The more-than-two-hour gap since the prior scheduled run remains unexplained.

While work is active, recover only after ten-minute staleness and only when no equivalent refresh is queued or running. Report observed dispatch latency; the configured cadence is not a hard freshness guarantee.

findings.text: The netip migration adds three binary-codec registrations and changes header initialization. Both comparison arms include the cheaper non-race registration from #15814. The retained netip sandbox experiment completed twelve batches of eight fresh starts per arm. Batch-mean medians are 288.4 ms for 6212e4f7b and 296.1 ms for 86ea1d1f3 (p=.590). Original processes, configuration, arithmetic and source/native inputs are independently verified. This frozen Go 1.27.0 comparison is inconclusive; it does not establish equivalence or current-upstream startup cost. No additional run was needed.

The matched current-source startup comparison is verified for 685d734a5 versus 91323cf62, including the split runsc/Sentry binaries and all eight release files. investigations.summary: The investigation and qualification are complete; upstream delivery is still pending in the linked PRs. Metric, tracereplay, trace and coretag corrections are published as #15930 and #15934–#15937. The full-unit trace failure was a fixture assertion applied to unrelated libc reads; its approved amendment is published and both full architecture owners plus analyzers pass. findings.text: At upstream master 9e9495997, Makefile retains the issue #10045 TODO and four explicit target exclusions. This confirms the remaining coverage gap; it does not establish that all of the original failures still reproduce.
Upstream a30d5fc67 fixed the metric NaN bucketer regression. The existing tests now pass 51 cases per architecture in one mixed-platform run; #15930 removes only the stale Make exclusion and ARM tag.

The tracereplay fixture exceeded the Unix-socket address limit under a long temporary directory. The existing replay test fails before and passes after the relative-path correction on AMD64 and ARM64, with no skips or missing results. #15934 removes its CI exclusion.

The coretag/trace baseline at de22cf145 selected four AMD64/ARM64 targets but executed none. Remote worker preparation failed while fetching the Ubuntu image token from auth.docker.io; all four results are missing. This is an infrastructure failure, not evidence of a coretag or trace test failure.

The later coretag-only run at 0838a53fc9 expected two owners and the native trace run at 4e31532a4 expected one; both executed zero tests because OCI preparation failed. The initial four-owner run also failed before runtime in both attempts. The trace-assertion correction is source-reviewed but not runtime-qualified.

The exact-image mirror discriminator reaches fresh compilation and both native coretag owners. Both TestEnable cases return ENODEV from the initial PR_SCHED_CORE_CREATE call, before sharing or cookie assertions, with no skips or missing results. This establishes a worker capability gap; the precise kernel configuration and topology were not collected. The production request must remain fail-closed.

findings.text: The unchanged AMD64 TestEnable passes in the existing KVM guest with CONFIG_SCHED_CORE=y and CPU0/CPU1 thread_siblings_list=0-1, within its original small-test timeout. Bare AMD64 and ARM64 worker ENODEV results remain retained; this supplies a capable test environment rather than changing production behavior. The ARM64 guest at 10f9151334 also passes unchanged TestEnable with no skips or missing results. Its actual console confirms aarch64, 4096-byte pages, CONFIG_SCHED_CORE=y and both CPUs sharing thread siblings 0-1; the remote action takes 16.748 seconds within the original 60-second limit.

Full ARM64 trace validation failed two pathname assertions because PointFchdir read an unused second syscall argument; fchdir only accepts an FD. A readable ignored argument makes both architecture regressions fail before the producer correction. Both complete native-namespace TestAll owners pass afterward with no skips or missing results. The assertion improvements and producer correction remain independent branches awaiting their review handoff.

Both independently reviewed trace changes are now ready upstream PRs. The exact-source runtime before/after results and owning AMD64/ARM64 analyzer checks are verified; no contributor decision remains for either PR.

The combined strict cohort passes both coretag guests, selection validation and owning AMD64/ARM64 Nogo checks. Both guests enforce CONFIG_SCHED_CORE=y and both CPU sibling lists equal 0-1. The separate raw-worker run skips both ENODEV owners and remains INCOMPLETE. Consumer audit finished at 23:31, well after the automatic 21:38 verdict; no reporting-latency improvement is claimed for those runs.

findings.text: The experiment still validates all 919 canonical owners and exactly the selected owner’s configuration and placement; the other 918 routes are explicitly unchecked. The selector and report-verifier suites pass 17 and 45 internal tests.
